abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:sec><jats:title>Key message</jats:title><jats:p>Quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping of 15 yield component traits in a German multi-founder population identified eight QTL each controlling ≥2 phenotypes, including the genetic loci<jats:italic>Rht24</jats:italic>,<jats:italic>WAPO-A1</jats:italic>and<jats:italic>WAPO-B1</jats:italic>.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Grain yield in wheat (<jats:italic>Triticum aestivum</jats:italic>L.) is a polygenic trait representing the culmination of many developmental processes and their interactions with the environment. Toward maintaining genetic gains in yield potential, ‘reductionist approaches’ are commonly undertaken by which the genetic control of yield components, that collectively determine yield, are established. Here we use an eight-founder German multi-parental wheat population to investigate the genetic control and phenotypic trade-offs between 15 yield components. Increased grains per ear was significantly positively correlated with the number of fertile spikelets per ear and negatively correlated with the number of infertile spikelets. However, as increased grain number and fertile spikelet number per ear were significantly negatively correlated with thousand grain weight, sink strength limitations were evident. Genetic mapping identified 34 replicated quantitative trait loci (QTL) at two or more test environments, of which 24 resolved into eight loci each controlling two or more traits—termed here ‘multi-trait QTL’ (MT-QTL). These included MT-QTL associated with previously cloned genes controlling semi-dwarf plant stature, and with the genetic locus<jats:italic>Reduced height 24</jats:italic>(<jats:italic>Rht24</jats:italic>) that further modulates plant height. Additionally, MT-QTL controlling spikelet number traits were located to chromosome 7A encompassing the gene<jats:italic>WHEAT ORTHOLOG OF APO1</jats:italic>(<jats:italic>WAPO-A1</jats:italic>), and to its homoeologous location on chromosome 7B containing<jats:italic>WAPO-B1</jats:italic>. The genetic loci identified in this study, particularly those that potentially control multiple yield components, provide future opportunities for the targeted investigation of their underlying genes, gene networks and phenotypic trade-offs, in order to underpin further genetic gains in yield.</jats:p></jats:sec>
title: Identification of eight QTL controlling multiple yield components in a German multi-parental wheat population, including Rht24, WAPO-A1, WAPO-B1 and genetic loci on chromosomes 5A and 6A
